newsitem.title: UK: British Building in profits after two yrs.
newsitem.headline: British Building in profits after two yrs.

text.p: British Building and Engineering Appliances Plc, facing a bid approach from the Britannia Group, reported a return to profitability for the first time in two years on Thursday.

The company, reported a thin profit of 24,000 stg on a turnover of 18.2 million for the six months to December 1996 but said it could offer a final dividend if its second half trade met its expectations.
On March 20, the company announced that it had received an approach from Britannia that may or may not lead to an offer for the company.
"Talks are still ongoing," the company's managing director David Hewlett told Reuters.
Hewlett also said that the company's operations had so far been "in line with expectations in the first three months of the second half.

The building services and equipment firm is currently executing a restructuring programme, under which it has already disposed off some of its small and high-risk businesses including plant hire and metal engineering.
Hewlett said the company would sell some more surplus properties to recover their book value of 1.7 million stg in cash.
The group's total borrowings were reduced by 0.9 million stg during the first half to 8.4 million and is expected to reduce "substantially" in the next one year, Hewlett said.

"Our second half trading performance has historically been our stronger period and this trend is expected to continue through receipts from trading and the proceeds from sale of surplus properties," the company's chairman John Joseph said.
Joseph said the firm would benefit from the current boost in the construction industry which, has recently got a boost by the Private Finance Initiative schemes and Millenium projects.
"All our businesses should benefit from increased activity in the coming months, as is indicated by improving levels of enquiries and coversions to secured orders," Joseph said.
British Building's share price closed at 64-1/2 pence on Wednesday.
